3. The case of the plaintiffs, in short, is that there was a Niskor Lakhiraj in the name of Ram Raton Sur under Bhulua Zamindari within Tauzi No. 5 of Noakhali Collectorate. The owner of the Niskor was Mohesh Chandra Narayan Chowdhury and subsequently Prasanna Narayan Chowdhury became owner of the Niskor by inheritance. The Niskor was subsequently sold in auction for arrears of cess and one Baksha Ali Mia Baksha Ali Patwary purchased the same in auction and got delivery of possession and sale certificate. The total area of this Niskor was 15 drones covering different mauzas. During the CS operation of 1915-1918 only 100.42 acres of land were recorded in CS Khatian No. 212 in respect of Ander Manik Mouza in the name of Baksha Ali Mia. The other lands of other Mouzas had no existence at that time. After the reformation of the land, the tenants did not return the land nor did they pay rent. Baksha Ali Patwary entered into possession of the entire land. After that, Baksha Ali Patwary made a gift of the entire Niskor land in favour of his two sons, namely, Eskabdor Ali Mia and Najibur Rahman @ Ali Ahmed Mia by a deed of gift dated 21st Bhadra 1320 BS. They gifted 1/3rd land of this Niskor in favour of their brother Sirajuddin Ahmed Mia by a deed of gift dated 21st Chaitra 1334 BS The sorts of Baksha Ali Mia made a settlement of 4 kanis of land of Ander Manik Mouza in favour of Abu Sayed Mohammad Noman by a kabuliyat dated 20th Poush 1358 BS corresponding to 5-1-1952 in respect of estate plot Nos. 17 and 21 of the Estate Map prepared by Elahi Baksha Amin. Abu Sayeed Mohammad Noman subsequently sold those 4 kanis of land to Anowar Ullah and Ahmed Ullah by a deed of sale dated 10-2-1952. Three sons of Baksha Ali Mia again made a settlement of 4 kanis of land of Ander Manik Mouza in favour of Abdur Rob in respect of estate plot Nos. 26 and 27. After that, Abdur Rob also sold those 4 kanis of land to Fazlul Haque and Hafizullah by a deed of sale dated 10-1-1952, and they sold those 4 kanis of land to Sultan Ahmed by a deed of sale dated 28-5-1958. Sultan Ahmed sold his 4 kanis of land to plaintiff No. 1, Zillur Rahim Mia by 2 deeds of sale dated 21-11-1967 and 30-11-1967. Thereafter, Hedayet Hussain, Abdul Kaiam and Anwarullah together sold their total 4 kanis of land to the plaintiffs by two deeds of sale dated 30-12-1967. Defendant Nos. 1 and 2 filed Title Suit No. 88 of 1963 in the Court of Sub-ordinate Judge (now Joint District Judge); Noakhali in respect of this suit land but the suit was dis-missed for default. The suit land was recorded during SA operation in Khatian Nos. 822 and 623 in the names of the plaintiffs' vendors. During Diara settlement, the names of the plaintiffs' vendors were recorded upto field stage but subsequently in the final Diara Khatian, the name of defendant No. 1 was recorded in respect of 13 annas and 15 gondas share of the suit land and the remaining 2 annas and 5 gondas share of land were recorded in the names of the plaintiffs. The Diara Khatian in the name of defendant No. 1 is wrong. Defendant No. 1 entered into the suit land as borgadar of the plaintiffs' vendors. Soon after their purchase, plaintiffs got possession in the suit land and possessed the same up to 1376 BS. But the defendants are not allowing the plain-tiffs to enter into the suit land from Ashar, 1377. The defendants have no right, title and interest in the suit land. Hence is the suit. 

 12. Admittedly there was a Niskor Taluk in the name of Mohesh Chandra Narayan Chowdhury within Bhulua Zamindary. There is no gainsaying the fact that the suit land is part of Niskor Taluk appertaining to Mouza Ander Manik. The plaintiffs' case is that the suit land appertains to estate plot Nos. 17, 21, 26 and 27 in the Estate Map prepared by Elahi Baksha Amin of Baksha Ali Estate. The defendants claimed that these estate plots attract the diara plot or the suit plots. In paragraph 8 of the written statement, the defendants stated to have purchased 6.64 acres of land of estate plot Nos. 9, 15, 21, 27, 10, 16, 22 and 28 of the Estate Map of the then Talukders. The deeds of sale, Exhibits A and A(1) of defendant No. 1 contain the above mentioned estate plots. Therefore, it appears that the estate plot Nos. 21 and 27 are common in both the lands. The plaintiffs' further case is that Mohesh Chandra Narayan Chowdhury gave an ejara of land of Ander Manik Mouza of the Niskor Taluk to one Ainuddin Patwary for 17 years for collection of rents from the tenants by patta kabuliyat dated 29th Poush 1292 BS marked as Exhibit-3, but before the expiry of this ejara period Mohesh Chandra Narayan Chowdhury created a Sarbapori Kayami Mokarary Taluk in respect of the land of this ejara patta, Exhibit 3, in the name of Baksha Ali Patwary by a patta dated 25th Agrahayan 1298 BS, marked Exhibit-2. The plaintiffs stated the origin of his suit land from Ejara patta dated 29th Poush 1292 BS (Exhibit-3). The plaintiff as PW 2 stated in his deposition that a Taluk, namely, Ainuddin Miajee was mentioned in Exhibit 3. Ainuddin Miajee as stated in the written statement of defendant No. 1 and Ainuddin Miajee as stated in Exhibit-3 is the same person. Exhibit-3 contains several Taluks and there is a mention of Taluk, Ainuddin Miajee and Omaruddin Hajee and from the above fact, it appears that the land contained in the deed of sale of defendant No. 1 got its origin in Exhibit-3. The plaintiff as PW2 in his cross-examination stated that Ainuddin had a son Ali Mia and that Ali Mia had two sons named Fazlul Haque and Sultan Ahmed. Defendant No. 1 stated to have purchased the suit land from Fazlul Haque and Sultan Ahmed by two registered deeds of sale dated 3-12-1957.
